sector.name: Co-Working
sector.description: Managed workspace operators serving enterprises and GCCs

sectorSummary.overview: All five operators described continued enterprise and GCC demand, with revenue growing across the group. Smartworks raised its FY27 revenue-growth target, while EFC’s Design & Build recovery and new-center occupancy remain important H2 execution tests.

trends.text: Enterprise and GCC demand remained a recurring source of leasing and workspace growth.
Operators continued to add or sign space and seats ahead of future revenue recognition.

tailwinds.text: Cross-sell, value-added services, fit-out or furniture offerings broadened revenue beyond core desk rentals.

headwinds.text: Recently added capacity requires occupancy and billing to ramp, so near-term margins or blended occupancy can fluctuate.

opportunities.text: Larger enterprise and GCC clients are supporting premium or multi-city managed-workspace formats.

risks.text: Expansion and fit-out spending precede revenue, making project timing, working capital and cash conversion key to H2 delivery.

insights.text: Smartworks raised its FY27 revenue-growth range to 33–35% from 28–30%.
EFC reaffirmed 50–60% FY27 Design & Build growth despite only about 17% H1 growth, leaving a pronounced H2 delivery requirement.

highlights: Operational supply reached ~174,000 seats across 254 centers; signed supply including LOIs was ~188,000 seats. Q2 added ~7,000 gross seats and exited ~2,200.

Transform was 93% third-party revenue; its order book and advance pipeline were ₹220 Cr. Quarterly revenue is milestone-dependent, so H1/order-book view is more informative.
About 57-58% of the ~3,000 seats vacated by an enterprise client were sold or committed; management expected 55-60% filled with revenue by December and said the balance pipeline was strong.
AWFIS Space Solutions Ltd.quote: “On profitability, we expect full-year cash EBITDA of INR 190 crores to INR 200 crores, with the second half stronger than the first as occupancy at recently launched centers continues to build and the premium cohort matures.”

AWFIS Space Solutions Ltd.whatChanged: Co-working demand and cash EBITDA strengthened in Q2, while project-timed Transform growth slowed; management reiterated its FY27 targets.
risks: Transform revenue depends on project-delivery milestones and grew only 16% in H1 against management’s around 20% FY27 ambition.
Recently opened centers need to ramp occupancy, and about 3,000 seats vacated by a large enterprise client were still being refilled.

fyPerformance: Q2 consolidated revenue from operations was ~₹332 Cr (+30% YoY), EBITDA ~₹134 Cr (+21%) and PAT ~₹77 Cr (+36%).

guidance.value: 50-60% YoY target; management said >₹300 Cr order book supports target

EFC (I) Ltd.outlook: Management expects annualized D&B growth of 50-60% in FY27, supported by a >₹300 Cr order book, while emphasizing project execution, external opportunities, collections and working-capital discipline. The transcript also gives 20-22% consolidated and various segment EBITDA margin figures, but their basis is not specified and they conflict with the reported 40% Q2 / 42% H1 margins; those margin figures are excluded from the draft guidance.
highlights: The three verticals grew, but D&B is project-driven and quarterly revenue varies by execution milestones; H1 growth remained below the stated full-year 50-60% target.
Management cited D&B order book above ₹300 Cr in Q&A as support for its FY27 target; earlier prepared remarks described D&B as an external, growing business.
Ultrafresh acquisition adds modular home-furniture products, North India manufacturing and 160+ customer touchpoints; management emphasized disciplined integration.
Proposed restructuring would separate leased managed-office operations from owned property activities; implementation is pending regulatory approvals.
Risks highlighted by management include working capital needs, execution and collections, project timing, inventory/capacity utilization, and higher material/service costs in Q2.
EFC (I) Ltd.quote: “Absolutely, we are on target to achieve the annual target that we have set for our Design & Build vertical.”
EFC (I) Ltd.whatChanged: H1 Design & Build growth was about 17% against the FY27 50–60% target, which management nevertheless reaffirmed on its order book.
risks: Design & Build delivery is concentrated in H2 and depends on conversion of the ₹300 Cr-plus order book.
Project collections and working capital require discipline as Furniture capacity and the Ultrafresh acquisition are integrated.
